findings.title: Release 1.75.4 · gorhill/uBlock
findings.summary_md: Raymond Hill released uBlock Origin 1.75.4 on November 3, 2026, with the change "Launch element picker only with a verified secret token." The release page points Firefox users to the AMO build and lists the tagged commit f417911. This was the first stable upstream release carrying the picker fix later tracked as GHSA-cmqw-9r2w-6wv2.

findings.title: Universal XSS from website-driven element picker · Advisory · gorhill/uBlock · GitHub
findings.summary_md: The uBlock Origin security advisory GHSA-cmqw-9r2w-6wv2, published by gorhill on November 15, 2026, rates the element picker universal XSS as High. It lists 1.75.2 and lower as affected and 1.75.4 as patched, and records that the reporter sent the flaw by email on November 1. The advisory traces the fix chain through the secret-token change in 1.75.4 and filter validation plus war:-filter blocking in 1.76.0 on November 8.

findings.title: Universal XSS in uBlock Origin from website-driven element picker
findings.summary_md: Smitty van Bodegom published the original write-up on November 15, 2026, describing a one-click universal XSS in the Firefox MV2 build of uBlock Origin. A page can recover the per-install extension UUID through a scriptlet, embed the element picker in an iframe set to opacity zero, and put a newline in the `opt` field so a second trusted scriptlet filter is created for an arbitrary domain. He notes that a filter recompile clears trust but that the attacker can open the target site immediately, and credits GPT-5.6 Sol with finding the issue.

findings.title: Tails 7.17.1
findings.summary_md: The Tails project published its 7.17.1 release note on November 17, 2026, calling it an emergency release that temporarily removes uBlock Origin from Tor Browser to fix a one-click universal XSS. The note says a malicious site can insert arbitrary JavaScript into any other site after a click, that Standard and Safer security levels are affected while Safest is not, and that no use in practice was known. It also updates the Linux kernel to 6.12.117 and says restarting Tails deletes any malicious uBlock Origin configuration inserted through the flaw.

findings.title: Tails 7.17.1 Removes uBlock Origin Over Critical One-Click XSS Flaw
findings.summary_md: Philipp Esselbach reported on November 17, 2026 that Tails removed uBlock Origin rather than ship a partial fix, even though the upstream correction already existed in 1.75.4. The article identifies GHSA-cmqw-9r2w-6wv2, describes the picker hijack and the trusted filter smuggled through a newline in the `opt` field, and explains the UUID leak via a default uAssets filter rule. It notes the Tails statement that no exploitation in practice was known and that a restart wipes the planted configuration.
